content_html:
The Inversion of Adaptation

When Secrecy Turns Dysfunctional

The evolutionary benefits of secrets, lies and deceit can become dysfunctional: Secrecy, lying, and deceit emerged as adaptive strategies in social evolution—ways to manage perception, negotiate risk, and stabilise groups. But every adaptive mechanism has a point of inversion, where continued use produces dysfunction. This coda models that inversion, specifies early warning signs, and offers practices for restoring healthy feedback to memory systems.

In primate cognition, tactical deception co‑evolves with lie detection—a social arms race that likely contributed to increasing neocortical complexity. Self‑deception may also confer short‑term advantages by masking cues, but accumulates long‑term costs if it blocks error correction.

Behaviour Adaptive Benefit Risk of Overuse
Secrecy Boundary hygiene; resource protection Isolation; fragmentation; paranoia
Lying Conflict mitigation; face‑saving Trust erosion; relational brittleness
Deceit Strategic negotiation; coalition building Exploitative dynamics; arms‑race escalation

Where Adaptation Flips to Dysfunction

Domain Adaptive Use Failure Mode Symptoms
Individual Emotion regulation via selective disclosure Self‑deception; dissociation Intrusions, moral dissonance, anxiety
Interpersonal Diplomacy; privacy Chronic mistrust Hypervigilance, rupture cycles
Collective Shared myth; cohesion Propaganda; historical amnesia Information silos, brittle identities
Cognitive Efficient prediction Model drift Reality mismatch, learned helplessness
  • Calibration loss: decreasing tolerance for disconfirming evidence.
  • Opacity creep: more secrets to protect earlier secrets.
  • Inconsistency inflation: rising cognitive load to maintain versions.
  • Feedback collapse: suppression of witnesses, logs, or audits.

Repair Heuristics (Ethical Feedback)

Practice Mechanism Where to Apply
Small, safe disclosures Re‑open reconsolidation with reduced threat Therapy; mediation; leadership forums
Version control for memory Track edits and rationales explicitly Personal journals; institutional archives
Counterfactual drills Stress‑test beliefs against alternatives Teams; policy design
Witness protocols Invite external challenge to narratives Truth‑and‑reconciliation; peer review
